stories.title: Tributes to 'kind, caring' woman found dead in Waterford
stories.summary: A woman in her 80s who was found dead at her Co Waterford home yesterday has been described as a "kind, caring and generous" person, whose loss will be felt by the community for a long time. The body of Noreen Daly, who was 81, was found at the house in a rural area at Ardsallagh near Youghal Bridge yesterday afternoon. A man in his 30s has been arrested as part of the investigation into her death. Ms Daly, a widow, is understood to have lived alone in the house and has been remembered as a kind person and a good neighbour who was heavily involved in the arts.

stories.title: Martin, Harris to back SF three-day wait abortion motion
stories.summary: The Taoiseach and Tánaiste are to both vote in favour of a Sinn Féin proposal to remove the mandatory three-day wait period for abortion in early pregnancy when it comes before the Dáil tomorrow. Mr Martin told Sinn Féin Leader Mary Lou McDonald that Minister for Health Jennifer Carroll MacNeill would likely introduce an amendment when the legislation is examined by an Oireachtas Committee, after the Dáil second-stage vote. Mr Martin said that he was aware of the arguments for and against the change and called for a respectful Dáil debate on the matter tonight. He said the people voted to repeal the 8th amendment in 2018 and to "provide free, safe and legal access to termination services".

stories.title: Russian ship fires warning shots at yacht near UK waters
stories.summary: Sailors on a Russian warship have fired warning shots at a UK-registered yacht that came near it in the English Channel. The incident, which occurred around 11.40am, is understood to have involved the Russian frigate Admiral Grigorovich in the sea between the Isle of Wight and Normandy. It is the latest sign of rising tensions between the UK and Russian President Vladimir Putin's country. There were no injuries and the yacht received no damage in the incident.

stories.title: Iran deal to be made public in coming days, says Trump
stories.summary: Doubts have swirled around the US-Iran interim deal to end the war in the Middle East with warnings that shipping and energy exports could take weeks to recover, although the US President Donald Trump said the text would be made public soon. The interim deal would extend a tenuous ceasefire announced in April by another 60 days and reopen the Strait of Hormuz, which Iran has effectively blocked since the US and Israel attacked Iran in February. Mr Trump said the text of the deal states clearly that Tehran will not have a nuclear weapon, and the full agreement would be made public in a formal setting in a few days. Speaking at the G7 meetings in France, Mr Trump added that he liked the idea of sending the Iran deal to the US Congress for review, a request by some Republican politicians.

stories.title: No reason for Donaldson complainants to lie, court told
stories.summary: There is no reason for two women who alleged they were abused by former DUP leader Jeffrey Donaldson as children to lie about what they experienced, his trial has been told. The remarks were made by prosecution counsel Rosemary Walsh KC as she finished her closing remarks to the jury of five women and seven men as the case in Newry Crown Court moves towards a conclusion. The former MP denies 18 charges, relating to the two complainants, including one count of rape on dates between 1985 and 2008. Mr Donaldson's barrister addressed the jury this afternoon. Kieran Vaughan KC told them they should set aside any personal opinion of Mr Donaldson or his politics. He said their duty was to decide the case on the evidence before them "without fear or favour".

stories.title: Hero's welcome as GAA superfan visits every Donegal club
stories.summary: A Donegal GAA fan with additional needs has completed the final leg of a journey that began two years ago - visiting every one of the 40 clubs in the north west county. Darragh Crawford, 24, returned this morning to a hero's welcome at his home club Naomh Pádraig in Lifford, having started his journey in Na Dúnaibh in 2024. He was given a guard of honour and presented with a Donegal GAA jersey, signed by all the team, a Naomh Pádraig jersey and a photograph of when he met the county team. What began as a personal ambition born from a deep love of Gaelic games grew into a story of perseverance, community spirit, and inclusion.
